record.original_question: Which k-orbit polytopes P admit a universal k-orbit extension, meaning a k-orbit extension of P that covers every other k-orbit extension of P?

evidence.quote: Problem 18. Which k-orbit polytopes P have a universal k-orbit extension that covers all other k-orbit extensions of P?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope is a ranked partially ordered set satisfying the standard axioms of diamond condition and strong flag-connectivity. Its automorphism group acts on the set of flags, and the polytope is called a k-orbit polytope when this action has exactly k orbits. Given two abstract polytopes P and Q, we say that Q is a (covering) extension of P, or that Q covers P, if there exists a surjective rank- and incidence-preserving map Q → P that is a covering in the standard sense (it maps flags to flags and is a bijection on the flags incident to each fixed flag of Q). A k-orbit extension of a k-orbit polytope P is an extension Q of P that is itself a k-orbit polytope.

A universal k-orbit extension of P is a k-orbit extension U of P such that for every k-orbit extension Q of P there exists a covering U → Q (so that U covers every other k-orbit extension of P).

Problem: Characterize the k-orbit polytopes P that admit a universal k-orbit extension.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a list of open problems on k-orbit polytopes (2018). A web search did not return any subsequent work resolving the existence/characterization of universal k-orbit extensions, and the topic remains an area of active research with no announced solution.
